correctness.rationale: For every finite connected unweighted bipartite graph, conjugation by bipartition signs transforms L=D-A into B=D+A. Expanding powers B through four proves exact entries by graph distance. Every distance-two term has quadratic discriminant at most -16s²<0; every edge cubic derivative has discriminant at most -s⁴/72<0 using (A³)uv≤d_ud_v and q≥s³/2. The scalar identity R4(x)=e^-x+∫_0^x e^{-(x-t)}t⁴/24 dt>0 and L positive semidefinite prove diagonal positivity. Distance-three entries are h³(4N-hW)/24, distance-four entries are h⁴(A⁴)uv/24>0, and all longer-distance entries vanish. Hence a finite minimum of unique positive edge and distance-three thresholds is necessary and sufficient with no later recovery. Standalone exact arithmetic checked 3249 connected labelled graphs of orders 2..6 at six rational timesteps and a separate seven-vertex double star, with 18537 discriminants; finite tests supplement the rigorous all-size proof.

value.rationale: This is a motivated complete local criterion for RK4 positivity in all irregular bipartite heat networks rather than a finite graph table or a minor parameter substitution. The proof identifies structurally enforced all-step positive distances 0,2,4, a universal no-recovery law, and two genuinely competing obstruction mechanisms: the path P6 is controlled by distance three at h=1/2, while the seven-vertex double star is controlled by an edge at approximately 0.430609<4/9. The exact threshold needs only local degrees and length-three walk counts, not global spectral computations.
